newsitem.title: JAPAN: G7 shares view stable forex market important - MOF.
newsitem.headline: G7 shares view stable forex market important - MOF.

text.p: The Group of Seven (G7) remains steadfast in its view that a stable foreign exchange market is important for the global economy, Japanese Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told reporters on Thursday.
"I think the G7 shares the view as before that a steady global economy and cooperation are important," Ogawa said.
"There is no change in our view that stable foreign exchange markets are important for a steady world economy," Ogawa said when asked about the G7 nations' stance on currencies.
In this light, Japan has maintained its stance that excessive weakness in the yen as well as excessive strength in the yen is undesirable, he added.
Central bank governors and finance ministers from the G7 members are meeting in Berlin on Saturday.

Asked about financial worries pushing down prices of bank shares, Ogawa said it will take time for the financial industry to adjust after disposing of its bad loan problems and to the proposed "Big Bang" financial reforms.
Ogawa said although each bank's case was different, "it is true that overall the bad loan problem is being dealt with steadily. It is also true we are heading towards stability and not uncertainty."
